messages:
maya: Heads-up — after last week's kernel-selection/batching tweak we've started seeing a handful of OOMs on r-s-03 during high prefix-churn traffic. Profiling shows eviction churn went up and GPU KV fragmentation spiked. attaching numbers.
sam: Can you paste the hot metrics? Hit-rate / evict/s / fragmentation %?
maya: sure — short summary:
```
host: r-s-03
window: 30m
prefix_hit_rate: 0.61 -> 0.47 (post-change)
evictions_per_min: 12 -> 48
gpu_free_mb: 2200 -> 900
frag_pct: 8.4 -> 29.7
oom_count (last 6h): 0 -> 3
```
maya: The kernel change reduced avg latency slightly but we lost compaction-friendly placement; prefill now scatters keys across slabs, increasing fragmentation and evictions. :grimacing:
jing: Two quick ideas — 1) entropy-aware eviction: compute per-prefix entropy (key diversity) and bias eviction away from low-entropy prefixes that are stable hotsets; 2) soft-ttl bump on newly-promoted keys to give warmup time before eviction.
alex: Entropy calc sounds neat, but what's the compute overhead and memory for maintaining per-prefix histograms at 99th percentile QPS? also how does it play with batching heuristics?
maya: Good Q. We experimented on dev: per-prefix sketch with fixed-size reservoir (128 samples) + approximate entropy produced useful signal with ~1-2% CPU and ~120KB per-cohort. We can aggregate by prefix-hash shard (coarse grain) to bound memory.
maya: For batching: preserve current continuous-batching but add a hint from cache tier: if request hits GPU-KV + batch-size > threshold, prefer kernel path A; else fallback. That reduces tail work.<priya: Nice. What guardrails/metrics should we watch during canary?>
priya: Metrics to watch: prefix_hit_rate, evictions_per_min, fragmentation_pct, gpu_free_mb, tail_latency p99, and # of async-prefetch ops queued.
sam: I can run a canary with these params: `entropy_protect_threshold=0.25`, `gpu_softcap=0.78`, `new_key_soft_ttl=6m`, `prefetch_async=true` on r-s-03 and r-s-07 staggered.
maya: SGTM. infra-bot, can you roll canary cfg to r-s-03 at next maintenance window and label it `entropy-guard-v1`? :pray:
infra-bot: deploy-bot: Applied config `entropy-guard-v1` to r-s-03 at 1754327005. Canary window starts now. Monitoring hooks created under /dashboards/eng-runtime/entropy-guard-v1.
sam: Starting traffic ramp. Will check back in 30m and 3h. revert criteria: >2 OOMs within 3h or evictions_per_min > 80 for 30m.
maya: If we see good behaviour we can test tightening kernel-batching threshold to reclaim some latency without reintroducing fragmentation. Also long-term: consider background compaction job to defragment GPU slabs during low-util windows.
jing: Also log suggestion: tag eviction events with prefix-hash and entropy score so we can correlate which cohorts cause churn. small change but huge for debugging.
priya: I'll update the experiment doc + rollback playbook. Thanks all — fingers crossed :crossed_fingers:
sam: quick note: if this reduces eviction churn we might be able to lower reserved GPU headroom by ~6% and save cost. win-win.
maya: +1. will post a short follow-up with first 3h metrics. thanks!
